/></mxCell><mxCell id="t2-c126" value="<b style="font-size:14px">How clients stay apart in a shared cell</b><br><span style="font-size:12px;color:#5b6675">1. Data, keys and models are separate Azure resources per client, in the client&#x27;s own resource group.<br>2. Each client has its own identities. Only id-&lt;client&gt;-app can use the client&#x27;s storage, vault and index;<br> only id-&lt;client&gt;-gw can call the client&#x27;s Azure OpenAI. Keys are off everywhere, so a token is the only way in.<br>3. The gateway API for a client accepts only that client&#x27;s app token and calls out only as that client&#x27;s gateway identity.<br>4. Container apps accept traffic only from the App Gateway subnet, so one client&#x27;s app can&#x27;t call another&#x27;s.<br>5. Per-client deployment identity: Contributor on its own resource group only. The cell identity has no data roles.<br>6. Terraform tests assert 1 to 5 for every client in the cell&#x27;s clients map.</span>" style="rounded=1;absoluteArcSize=1;arcSize=12;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#c0392b;strokeWidth=2;align=left;verticalAlign=top;spacingLeft=6;spacingTop=0;spacingRight=4;fontColor=#1b2430;" vertex="1" parent="t2"><mxGeometry x="3470.0" y="1740.0" width="803" height="148" as="geometry" /></mxCell><mxCell id="t2-c127" value="<b style="font-size:14px">What it costs (approx. list price, USD/month)</b><br><span style="font-size:12px;color:#5b6675">Shared per cell: App Gateway WAF_v2 ~400, APIM ~700 (Standard v2*), AI Search S1 x2 ~490,<br>Container Apps environment ~0 idle, cell Log Analytics ~50. About 1,650 per cell.<br>Per client: 3 private endpoints ~22, logs ~25, an always-on replica ~40, tokens as used.<br>About 90 per client + 1,650 / clients in the cell. At 20 clients: ~170 per client.<br>*Premium APIM (internal VNet mode, as built today) is ~2,800: ~280 per client at 20.<br>Tier 1 is ~700 to ~1,400 per client before tokens (~3,500 with a Premium gateway).</span>" style="rounded=1;absoluteArcSize=1;arcSize=12;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#c3cad4;strokeWidth=1.2;align=left;verticalAlign=top;spacingLeft=6;spacingTop=0;spacingRight=4;fontColor=#1b2430;" vertex="1" parent="t2"><mxGeometry x="4288.0" y="1740.0" width="803" height="148" as="geometry" /></mxCell><mxCell id="t2-c128" value="<b style="font-size:14px">Fits / doesn&#x27;t fit</b><br><span style="font-size:12px;color:#5b6675">Fits: confidential client data where the contract accepts shared, Microsoft-managed<br>compute and edge, but wants dedicated data stores, keys, models and logs. Most hosted<br>solutions. Onboarding in hours, not days: no vending, no new gateway.<br>Doesn&#x27;t fit: contracts that require a dedicated subscription, network-level separation,<br>their own ExpressRoute path with per-client firewall rules, or PTU capacity of their own.<br>Those clients stay on Tier 1. Moving up is a data copy plus a new stamp.</span>" vertex="1" parent="t3"><mxGeometry x="6708.0" y="1265.0" width="24" height="24" as="geometry" /></mxCell><mxCell id="t3-c79" value="<b style="font-size:14px">Why a bug in the pooled app can&#x27;t read another tenant&#x27;s documents</b><br><span style="font-size:12px;color:#5b6675">A contoso user&#x27;s token carries role Tenant.contoso and group sg-aiadv-contoso-users. The app exchanges it (on-behalf-of) for a storage token and a search token that are still that user&#x27;s.<br>Storage holds a role assignment for sg-aiadv-contoso-users on container &#x27;contoso&#x27; only; Search on index &#x27;contoso&#x27; only. If the code asks for container &#x27;adatum&#x27;, Azure returns 403.<br>The app&#x27;s own managed identity has NO data role on storage or search. It only pulls images and writes telemetry. Model calls carry the user&#x27;s token to the gateway, which keys token limits on Tenant.&lt;code&gt;.</span>" style="rounded=1;absoluteArcSize=1;arcSize=12;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#c0392b;strokeWidth=2;align=left;verticalAlign=top;spacingLeft=6;spacingTop=0;spacingRight=4;fontColor=#1b2430;" vertex="1" parent="t3"><mxGeometry x="6750.0" y="1377.0" width="1060" height="132" as="geometry" /></mxCell><mxCell id="t3-c80" value="<b style="font-size:14px">What is weaker than Tiers 1 and 2 (say it first)</b><br><span style="font-size:12px;color:#5b6675">One process serves every tenant: a memory or cache bug could mix answers. Mitigated by tenant + user<br>cache keys and no semantic cache, not eliminated. One Azure OpenAI quota and one outage domain for<br>all tenants; gateway limits keep it fair. No per-tenant network path or CMK on logs. A regulator or<br>client who asks &#x27;is anything of ours processed alongside other clients?&#x27; gets a yes.</span>" style="rounded=1;absoluteArcSize=1;arcSize=12;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#c0392b;strokeWidth=2;align=left;verticalAlign=top;spacingLeft=6;spacingTop=0;spacingRight=4;fontColor=#1b2430;" vertex="1" parent="t3"><mxGeometry x="6050.0" y="1630.0" width="803" height="116" as="geometry" /></mxCell><mxCell id="t3-c81" value="<b style="font-size:14px">What it costs (approx. list price, USD/month)</b><br><span style="font-size:12px;color:#5b6675">Shared per pool: App Gateway ~400, APIM ~700 (Standard v2*), Search S1 x2 ~490, app replicas ~120,<br>Log Analytics ~80, Azure OpenAI pay per token. About 1,800 per pool.<br>Per tenant: a container, an index, an encryption scope, a group, a job identity: ~5 + tokens.<br>At 45 tenants (the cap, under S1&#x27;s 50 indexes): ~45 per tenant. Onboarding: same day.<br>*Premium APIM (internal VNet mode, as built today) is ~2,800: ~90 per tenant at 45.</span>" style="rounded=1;absoluteArcSize=1;arcSize=12;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#c3cad4;strokeWidth=1.2;align=left;verticalAlign=top;spacingLeft=6;spacingTop=0;spacingRight=4;fontColor=#1b2430;" vertex="1" parent="t3"><mxGeometry x="6868.0" y="1630.0" width="803" height="116" as="geometry" /></mxCell><mxCell id="t3-c82" value="<b style="font-size:14px">Fits / doesn&#x27;t fit</b><br><span style="font-size:12px;color:#5b6675">Fits: internal Chatham tools, standard-content products (market commentary, rate and hedge<br>explainers over Chatham&#x27;s own research), trials and proofs of concept, small clients whose<br>data classification is internal or public and whose contract allows logical isolation.<br>Doesn&#x27;t fit: confidential client documents, client-specific models or fine-tunes, PTU, CMK<br>requirements on everything, or a client-owned network path. Those go to Tier 2 or Tier 1.</span>" Tier 2: shared cell. Shared front door, compute and AI gateway; every client keeps its own data, keys, models and identities

ADR 0014. One subscription (a 'cell') holds up to 20 clients. What's shared processes client traffic but stores none of it; everything that stores client data is per client and only that client's identities can use it.

How clients stay apart in a shared cell
1. Data, keys and models are separate Azure resources per client, in the client's own resource group.
2. Each client has its own identities. Only id-<client>-app can use the client's storage, vault and index;
only id-<client>-gw can call the client's Azure OpenAI. Keys are off everywhere, so a token is the only way in.
3. The gateway API for a client accepts only that client's app token and calls out only as that client's gateway identity.
4. Container apps accept traffic only from the App Gateway subnet, so one client's app can't call another's.
5. Per-client deployment identity: Contributor on its own resource group only. The cell identity has no data roles.
6. Terraform tests assert 1 to 5 for every client in the cell's clients map.
What it costs (approx. list price, USD/month)
Shared per cell: App Gateway WAF_v2 ~400, APIM ~700 (Standard v2*), AI Search S1 x2 ~490,
Container Apps environment ~0 idle, cell Log Analytics ~50. About 1,650 per cell.
Per client: 3 private endpoints ~22, logs ~25, an always-on replica ~40, tokens as used.
About 90 per client + 1,650 / clients in the cell. At 20 clients: ~170 per client.
*Premium APIM (internal VNet mode, as built today) is ~2,800: ~280 per client at 20.
Tier 1 is ~700 to ~1,400 per client before tokens (~3,500 with a Premium gateway).
Fits: confidential client data where the contract accepts shared, Microsoft-managed
compute and edge, but wants dedicated data stores, keys, models and logs. Most hosted
solutions. Onboarding in hours, not days: no vending, no new gateway.
Doesn't fit: contracts that require a dedicated subscription, network-level separation,
their own ExpressRoute path with per-client firewall rules, or PTU capacity of their own.
Those clients stay on Tier 1. Moving up is a data copy plus a new stamp.
Shared in the cell: carries client traffic, stores none
Per client: client data, keys, models, identities
User path: client network -> hub firewall -> shared App Gateway (listener per client) -> client's app
Model path: client's app -> shared AI gateway (client's API) -> client's own Azure OpenAI
Data path: client's app identity -> its own storage, vault and search index (private endpoints)
Egress: cell workload subnets -> hub firewall (UDR)
Private Link: client's own Azure VNet -> private endpoint -> cell App Gateway Private Link
Sources: docs/adr/0014-isolation-tiers.md, docs/architecture/isolation-tiers.md, terraform/stamps/cell, terraform/stamps/cell-client. Names and addresses are the example configs.
One app for many tenants; Azure checks the signed-in user's own token on every data call
~USD 45 per tenant a month at 45 per pool · public and internal data only · blast radius: 45 tenants
Boundary: the user's token; the app itself has no data role. Terraform: stamps/pool
Tier 3: pooled. One multi-tenant app for many clients; Azure enforces each client's data partition on the signed-in user's own token

Why a bug in the pooled app can't read another tenant's documents
A contoso user's token carries role Tenant.contoso and group sg-aiadv-contoso-users. The app exchanges it (on-behalf-of) for a storage token and a search token that are still
Storage holds a role assignment for sg-aiadv-contoso-users on container 'contoso' only; Search on index 'contoso' only. If the code asks for container 'adatum', Azure returns
The app's own managed identity has NO data role on storage or search. It only pulls images and writes telemetry. Model calls carry the user's token to the gateway, which keys
What is weaker than Tiers 1 and 2 (say it first)
One process serves every tenant: a memory or cache bug could mix answers. Mitigated by tenant + user
cache keys and no semantic cache, not eliminated. One Azure OpenAI quota and one outage domain for
all tenants; gateway limits keep it fair. No per-tenant network path or CMK on logs. A regulator or
client who asks 'is anything of ours processed alongside other clients?' gets a yes.
What it costs (approx. list price, USD/month)
Shared per pool: App Gateway ~400, APIM ~700 (Standard v2*), Search S1 x2 ~490, app replicas ~120,
Log Analytics ~80, Azure OpenAI pay per token. About 1,800 per pool.
Per tenant: a container, an index, an encryption scope, a group, a job identity: ~5 + tokens.
At 45 tenants (the cap, under S1's 50 indexes): ~45 per tenant. Onboarding: same day.
*Premium APIM (internal VNet mode, as built today) is ~2,800: ~90 per tenant at 45.
Fits: internal Chatham tools, standard-content products (market commentary, rate and hedge
explainers over Chatham's own research), trials and proofs of concept, small clients whose
data classification is internal or public and whose contract allows logical isolation.
Doesn't fit: confidential client documents, client-specific models or fine-tunes, PTU, CMK
requirements on everything, or a client-owned network path. Those go to Tier 2 or Tier 1.
Shared by every tenant in the pool
User path: one host name -> pool App Gateway -> pooled app (tenant from the token)
Data path on the user's own token: Azure checks container- and index-scoped roles
Model path: user's token -> AI gateway (per-tenant limits) -> shared Azure OpenAI
Ingestion: per-tenant job identity -> that tenant's container and index only
Egress: pool workload subnets -> hub firewall (UDR)
Sources: docs/adr/0014-isolation-tiers.md, docs/architecture/isolation-tiers.md, terraform/stamps/pool. Names are the example config.

Fixed costs are approximate US list prices (USD/month), with Standard v2 API Management, to show the shape of the saving. Details, cost math and the trade-offs of each tier: docs/architecture/isolation-tiers.md. Generated by generate_side_by_side.py from the three tier diagrams.
